benchmark.category: a Telegram affiliate deal-reposting tool with an admin panel and a private channel reader
benchmark.users: a Flipkart affiliate deal poster who runs Telegram deal channels (@dealfetch, Deltfetch) and reposts deals picked up from other people's deal channels

requirements.statement: On the /admin Telegram login panel, activating 'resend code' asks the server for a fresh login code and opens a new code input box that takes typed input
requirements.notes: The user asked for a fresh code twice; the box and the request are one observable action on the admin screen.

requirements.statement: POST /api/public/telegram/resend-code requests a fresh login code from Telegram using the stored API id/hash and phone number and reports whether it was requested, returning an error naming the reason instead of a success when the credentials are wrong or Telegram refuses
requirements.notes: The code request goes through Telegram's own service; a false success here is what strands the user.

requirements.statement: The Telegram login code box stays on screen until the user submits or cancels, accepts the code typed into it and submits it, disables the submit control while the request is in flight, and on an error keeps the box open showing the message
requirements.notes: The user's complaint was that the box disappeared before they could type; the control must be operable and answer on screen.

requirements.statement: POST /api/public/telegram/verify-code with a valid code signs the stored Telegram user account in and persists the session so the admin panel reports it connected after a reload, and a wrong or empty code is refused with an error that leaves the account signed out
requirements.notes: A code accepted in the browser but not stored is the failure the user hit repeatedly.

requirements.statement: The admin settings form lets the user overwrite the Telegram api id, api hash, 2FA password and phone number and save them, and after saving the screen shows the newly entered values
requirements.notes: 'harsh code' read as the Telegram two-factor password; the user wants to replace details previously entered wrong.

requirements.statement: PUT /api/public/settings stores telegram_api_id, telegram_api_hash, telegram_2fa_password and telegram_phone, and a new admin session reading the settings receives the newly saved values rather than the previous ones
requirements.notes: The point of re-entering is that the old wrong values are gone; a save that keeps the old value fails the user's intent.

requirements.statement: After the affiliate API keys are saved in the admin panel, the next conversion request uses them from the stored settings without a server restart and returns a converted link rather than an authentication error
requirements.notes: 'please continue' means the saved keys take effect immediately.

requirements.statement: A background status poll or page re-render on /admin does not close, clear or replace the open Telegram code box while the user is typing into it
requirements.notes: Build description: the code box was skipped four times while the agent waited; the paranoid half of 'give me that box' is that it survives re-renders.

requirements.statement: Repeated 'resend code' requests within a short window are throttled and answer with a message telling the user to wait rather than sending another code to Telegram
requirements.notes: Agent reported that extra code requests can get the number locked, which would also break the live site; the refusal must be visible, not silent.

requirements.statement: After a successful code login, reloading /admin and re-reading the reader status reports the Telegram account connected with its stored user and does not ask for another code
requirements.notes: Build description: the reader runs on a saved Telegram user-account session that must survive the admin reload the operator does anyway.

requirements.statement: A conversion attempted with a placeholder or rejected affiliate key returns an error naming the failure and produces no link, rather than a canned or synthesised link
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of 'keys are saved': the failure path of a bad key must not look like success.

requirements.statement: The caption built for a deal states the product title, the price in rupees, the SuperCoins cashback, the seller name and the user's own fkrt.co link, and each of those equals the value stored for that deal
requirements.notes: Build description: the 'Supercoin Deals' / 'Flipkart Deal' caption contract; the check is value-equals-stored-value for every field the caption shows.

requirements.statement: A destination configured with min_price 4500 receives no deal priced at or below ₹4,500, while a destination configured with min_price 0 receives the same deal
requirements.notes: Build description: Deltfetch keeps the old script's >₹4,500 filter while @dealfetch takes everything; the boundary value must be checked on both sides.

requirements.statement: When the ExtraPe conversion fails the app converts the same product code through Sankmo and stores the resulting link, and a second conversion of that product code reuses the cached link without calling the provider again
requirements.notes: Build description: ExtraPe with Sankmo fallback and a converted-link cache; both the fallback and the cache hit must be observable.

requirements.statement: A deal whose product code was already sent to a destination is not sent to that destination a second time across reader cycles, and one deal produces exactly one post per destination
requirements.notes: Agent reported @dealfetch already gets duplicate posts from two posting systems; the reader must not add a third.

requirements.statement: A source post containing an fkrt.site or fkrtt.in link is resolved to its Flipkart product code before conversion, and a post with no resolvable product code is skipped and recorded without an error post to the destination
requirements.notes: Build description: extraction of product codes or resolution of shortened affiliate links.

requirements.statement: Editing a source post after the reader has read it does not add a new post to a destination and does not alter an already-sent post
requirements.notes: Build description: edits to source posts are explicitly ignored; success here is no new post.

requirements.statement: The /admin page renders its tabs, status cells and settings form fully visible and unclipped at desktop and phone widths, with text meeting a recognised contrast ratio against its background and primary actions visible without opening a dialog
requirements.notes: Tier 2 layout class; the operator works on this panel from a phone as well as a desktop.

requirements.statement: Saving the reader settings shows a success message naming what was saved, and a rejected save shows the reason in the user's terms while leaving the previously loaded values in the form
requirements.notes: Nothing may save silently or fail silently on the settings form.

requirements.statement: The Channel Reader tab on /admin shows the reader's enabled state, connected state, Telegram user, source channels, last read time, last sent time and last error, each showing a stored value or an explicit 'never'/dash rather than an empty cell
requirements.notes: Build description: reader-connected, reader-sources, reader-last-read, reader-last-sent, reader-last-error cells; the empty state is part of the requirement.

requirements.statement: GET /api/public/reader/status returns enabled, connected, user, sources[], last_read, last_sent and last_error with the stored values, and null or an explicit never for a timestamp that has not happened yet
requirements.notes: Field list taken from the build description; the status must reflect the running reader, not a fixed placeholder.

requirements.statement: A failed read or post records its message in last_error and the status endpoint returns it, and a later success does not erase the fact that the failure happened without a newer timestamp replacing it
requirements.notes: Otherwise the operator cannot tell a working reader from one silently erroring every cycle.

requirements.statement: Toggling the reader on/off switch changes the switch's own state and the status shown beside it, and after a page reload the switch reflects the stored value while the Telegram account still reports connected
requirements.notes: A control that renders must do the thing and change itself; toggling must not disturb the stored Telegram session.

requirements.statement: PUT /api/public/settings with reader_enabled false stops the reader cycle and true starts it, and the stored boolean is what the next status read reports
requirements.notes: The switch must act on the server loop, not only on the browser.

requirements.statement: Every admin tab, including the Channel Reader tab and the Converter History tab, opens from /admin, from a direct reload of that page and after signing in again, and renders its own content with no blank panel or crash
requirements.notes: Build description names admin-tab-reader as a tab among existing ones; regression across tabs is what the user keeps using.

requirements.statement: GET /api/public/settings and the reader/status reads behind the tabs return the stored data for a signed-in admin, and a request with no session returns 401 so the page can send the user to the login screen instead of rendering empty panels
requirements.notes: A tab that renders is only as good as the data call behind it.

requirements.statement: The Converter History tab lists previously converted links with their source and time, newest first, shows an explicit empty message when nothing has been converted, and stays usable when the list grows past a thousand rows
requirements.notes: Build description lists Converter History as an existing surface that must keep working; zero rows and many rows are the two states to check.

requirements.statement: The conversion history endpoint returns each converted link once with its original and converted form and timestamp, scoped to the signed-in admin's own data, and a reload or new session returns the same rows
requirements.notes: History that lives only in the browser would lose the operator's record on reload.

requirements.statement: The /admin route shows the password-only login form to a visitor with no session, and after a successful sign-in renders the admin tabs rather than an empty page
requirements.notes: Product shell: the panel is password-only, so the route must gate and then render.

requirements.statement: POST /api/public/auth/login with password RadheKrishna@#12 returns a session token that unlocks the admin endpoints, and a wrong password is refused with an error and no token
requirements.notes: Seed credential supplied by the build: Admin password RadheKrishna@#12. Every later phase signs in with exactly this value.

requirements.statement: GET /api/public/reader/status without a valid admin token returns 401 and none of the reader fields (user, sources, timestamps, last_error), and with a valid token returns them
requirements.notes: The status exposes the owner's Telegram account name; both the refusal and the legitimate read are checked.

requirements.statement: The Telegram bot token, Telegram api hash, ExtraPe key, Sankmo key and the admin password never appear in any API response, page source or browser-visible state, and a request that would return them is refused
requirements.notes: The reader status and settings pages are the likely leak points.

requirements.statement: The admin panel offers a Disconnect action for the stored Telegram account that asks for confirmation, and afterwards the reader status shows connected false while the saved credentials stay on file
requirements.notes: Build description: a 'Sankmo Disconnect' control exists; the paranoid half of a stored login is a deliberate way to end it.

requirements.statement: The disconnect endpoint ends the stored Telegram session, persists the disconnected state, and the next status read reports connected false with no session string still usable for reading or posting
requirements.notes: A disconnect that leaves the session valid would let the reader keep reading after the operator revoked it.

requirements.statement: The Channel Reader settings form exposes the caption, the source channel list, up to five destination chat names with a minimum price each, the posting bot selector, a photo-mode switch and a save control, and after saving and reloading it shows the saved values
requirements.notes: Build description names reader-caption-input, reader-sources-input, reader-dest-chat-N, reader-dest-min-N, reader-bot-select, reader-photo-switch and reader-settings-save.

requirements.statement: PUT /api/public/settings persists reader_caption, reader_sources, reader_destinations (chat name plus min_price, at most five), the posting bot, photo mode and the enabled flag, and GET returns them identically in a new admin session
requirements.notes: Every field the screen sends must be a field the API stores and returns.

requirements.statement: PUT /api/public/settings refuses a reader_enabled that is not a boolean, a reader_sources entry that is not a valid channel name (for example 'a b!'), more than five reader_destinations, and a min_price that is not a number, and stores nothing at all when it refuses
requirements.notes: A half-written settings row would leave the reader pointing at a broken channel; the refusal must be whole.

requirements.statement: Each saved destination is stored and returned as https://t.me/<name> whatever form of the name was typed, and a destination entered twice appears once
requirements.notes: Otherwise the same channel could take two posts of the same deal.

requirements.statement: A fresh install's stored settings carry reader_sources hotdealsbywd, tapworthy and Flipkart_scdeals_PranayCC, with a @dealfetch destination at min_price 0 and a Deltfetch destination at min_price 4500, and the reader status reports those sources
requirements.notes: Seed values named in the build context as the defaults to restore; later phases seed from exactly these.

requirements.statement: A saved reader setting reads back byte-for-byte after a page reload and in a brand-new admin session, and a settings write that fails leaves the previous values intact
requirements.notes: Persistence across sessions is the only proof the save reached the store.

requirements.statement: With photo mode on, the posted deal carries the deal image with the same caption text, and when the image cannot be fetched the post still goes out as a text post with that caption instead of failing or posting an empty photo
requirements.notes: Build description: optional photo mode alongside the default text-only post; the fallback is what keeps a deal from being lost.

requirements.statement: A deal that clears every destination's minimum price is posted to both @dealfetch and Deltfetch in the same cycle, the result of each post is recorded separately, and one destination failing records its error while the other post still lands
requirements.notes: Build description: parallel posting to both channels with an optional photo; a single shared success flag would hide a failed channel.

requirements.statement: Posting reads the bot token from the server-side configuration, and with no token or a rejected token the post fails with an error recorded in the reader status and shown in the admin, never reported as sent
requirements.notes: The preview has no converter bot token, so a silent fake success is the failure mode to catch; the vitest mock does not prove the live path.

requirements.statement: When ExtraPe and then Sankmo time out, rate-limit or return an error, the conversion reports the failure to the caller in the user's terms and no deal is posted with a broken or empty link
requirements.notes: Third-party integration class: the app must stay responsive and must not invent a link.

requirements.statement: Each reader cycle reads each configured source channel once and a new cycle does not start while one is still running, so a deal found in two source channels in one cycle is still posted once
requirements.notes: Overlapping cycles are the ordinary way a de-duplicated reader still double-posts.

requirements.statement: The project type-checks with no errors and the full test run passes, including the private-reader format test, the mocked pipeline flow test and the existing suite
requirements.notes: Build description names yarn exec tsc --noEmit, the two reader vitest files and yarn test as the checks to run.

requirements.statement: The Channel Reader tab shows, for each source channel, when it was last read and whether that read succeeded, so the operator can see which channel stopped producing deals
requirements.notes: benchmark: channel-monitoring tools show per-source health, not one global last-read time

requirements.statement: The operator can add a new source channel and remove an existing one from the settings form, and the change applies on the next reader cycle without restarting the server
requirements.notes: benchmark: admin tools let the operator change the watched set themselves

requirements.statement: The settings form previews the caption the bot will publish, rendered from the saved template with a sample deal, before the operator saves it
requirements.notes: benchmark: posting tools preview the message the audience will see

requirements.statement: The Converter History tab lets the operator filter by product code or link and copy a converted link from its row, and the filtered count equals the rows shown
requirements.notes: benchmark: link-conversion tools let the operator find an earlier conversion and reuse its link
